Osmotic energy, also known as blue energy, is a promising method for creating renewable electricity from the natural mixing of saltwater and freshwater.

However, this technology has long faced a major barrier: the membranes designed to capture this energy either allow ions to pass through quickly but fail to separate charges effectively, or they excel at charge separation but work at a very slow rate.
Under normal conditions, these nanopores allow ions to pass through with high precision but at a very slow pace.
When applied to the nanopores, these outward-facing heads attract an extremely thin layer of water, just a few molecules thick.
This breakthrough brings efficient and practical osmotic power stations one step closer to reality.
